notes:
I couldn't do this research this time, so I have no verse notes for Amos 4 to give you.

My first attempt to open several commentary pages at once went over the tool's usage limit. After that I tried to open the Enduring Word page directly, but the tool refused because the address hadn't come from a search first. My next search was blocked because I had no tool calls left. No page loaded, so I have nothing sourced to report. Your rules say not to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything from memory.

If you start a new request, I'll fetch the pages one at a time, starting with a search so each address is accepted. In order, I'd go through:

1. **Verse-by-verse readings:** Enduring Word (Guzik), Precept Austin, and the Bible Hub / StudyLight entries for Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Gill and Wesley's Notes on Amos 4.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** the most likely places are v. 4–5 (worship without obedience), v. 6–11 (whether God sends disasters to bring people back) and v. 12 ("prepare to meet your God"). I'd check Spurgeon, Desiring God, Ligonier/The Gospel Coalition, Seedbed, the LCMS and 1517 for sermons on these verses.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, what "Harmon" in v. 3 means), and New Advent / Catholic.com for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'd include prosperity or similar popular teaching only if the allowed sites actually discuss it.

You could also split the job, for example v. 1–5 first and v. 6–13 second, which keeps each request well within the limit.
